questions.questionText: What does a BLACK flag in the PLA warning system indicate?

questions.referenceSection: Hazards / Warnings - PLA WARNING FLAG SYSTEM

questions.questionText: Under a RED PLA warning flag, what specific advice is given to man-powered vessels?

Man-powered vessels navigate with extreme caution
Schools and novices not to go afloat on ebb tide
Man-powered vessels should find safe mooring

questions.questionText: For approximately how long each side of high tide are the Richmond Weir sluice gates raised, allowing free navigation?

questions.questionText: What conditions can dramatically change the period of free navigation at Richmond Lock?
questions.correctAnswer: Drought conditions and high fluvial flow
options: Drought conditions and high fluvial flow
questions.explanation: In drought conditions, the gates will be closed for longer periods, whilst in periods of high fluvial flow they may remain open for much longer.
questions.referenceSection: The Locks - Richmond Lock and Weir

questions.questionText: Which vessels are exempt from the navigation exclusion zone at Richmond Lock when weirs are lowered?
questions.correctAnswer: Vessels manoeuvring on Lock island berths, emergency vessels, and smaller vessels using No. 1 arch boat rollers
options: Vessels manoeuvring on Lock island berths, emergency vessels, and smaller vessels using No. 1 arch boat rollers
Only RNLI lifeboats and PLA vessels
Vessels with prior permission from the Lock Foreman
questions.explanation: Only vessels manoeuvring on or to Lock island berths, vessels engaged in emergency operations, or smaller vessels wishing to utilise the boat rollers in No. 1 arch are exempt from the exclusion zone.
questions.referenceSection: The Locks - Richmond Lock and Weir

questions.questionText: What does the PLA flag warning system specifically warn about?
questions.correctAnswer: Potentially fast ebb tidal flows due to higher fluvial flow
options: Potentially fast ebb tidal flows due to higher fluvial flow
Rising water levels due to storm surges
questions.explanation: The PLA operate a flag system to warn about potentially fast ebb tidal flows, where the flow is increased because of higher fluvial (non-tidal) flow.
questions.referenceSection: Hazards / Warnings - PLA WARNING FLAG SYSTEM

questions.questionText: Under a GREEN PLA flag, what specific advice is given to all river users?
questions.correctAnswer: Navigate with caution and maintain a proper look out
options: Navigate with caution and maintain a proper look out
Man-powered vessels should stay close to the bank
All vessels should reduce speed to minimum steerage
questions.explanation: A GREEN flag indicates Average Fluvial Flows. All river users should navigate with caution and maintain a proper look out.
questions.referenceSection: Hazards / Warnings - PLA WARNING FLAG SYSTEM

questions.questionText: Under a YELLOW PLA flag, who should 'navigate with extreme caution and consider whether it is safe to go afloat on the ebb tide'?
questions.correctAnswer: All river users of man-powered vessels
options: All river users of man-powered vessels
All river users including powered vessels
questions.explanation: Under YELLOW flag, ALL river users of man-powered vessels should navigate with extreme caution and consider whether it is safe for them to go afloat on the ebb tide.
questions.referenceSection: Hazards / Warnings - PLA WARNING FLAG SYSTEM

questions.questionText: When yellow boards showing 'CAUTION STREAM DECREASING' are displayed at locks, what are unpowered boats advised to do?
questions.explanation: When yellow 'CAUTION STREAM DECREASING' boards are displayed, unpowered boats are still advised not to navigate, while powered boats may navigate with caution.
